board_convention: 6 rows x 7 columns; row 0 is the TOP row, row 5 is the BOTTOM row (gravity fills bottom-up). Each row is a 7-character string using '.', 'X', 'O'. Load with game_engine.board_from_rows(rows).

states.description: Standard empty opening board. Use for the Human vs easy-AI and Human vs stronger-AI demos by changing only the AI's search depth (and, once implemented, comparing minimax vs alphabeta).

O has three in a row at row 5, columns 0-2, and threatens an immediate win by playing column 3. X has two in a row at row 5, columns 4-5 (not yet urgent). A shallow/greedy agent that only scores the current position may miss the threat and develop its own line (for example column 6) instead of blocking; an agent that looks at least one opponent reply ahead must block at column 3. Use this state to show that different search depths choose different moves.

Midgame position with all seven columns still open and no immediate win, giving a large branching factor. Use this state to compare the number of nodes expanded by plain Minimax versus Minimax with Alpha-Beta pruning at the same depth (the required alpha-beta node-reduction demo).

Column 3 is completely full (alternating X/O, no winner). legal_moves(board) must exclude column 3, and apply_move(board, 3, player) must raise ValueError instead of crashing or silently corrupting the board. This is the engine-level failure/edge-case demo.
